text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for service=model-serving-runtime in prod (us-west1). 5xx spike from 0.2% -> 6.4% over 3m. Pager fired for @maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): ack, I'm on it. pulling dashboard + logs.

eng-runtime: thx — suspected OOM/segfault in model-runner based on similar pattern earlier. can you grab recent model-runner pod logs and core dumps?

maya (oncall): running quick checks
```bash
kubectl -n prod logs deploy/model-runner -l app=model-runner --tail=200 | grep -iE "segfault|oom|killed" -n || true
```

maya (oncall): got output snippet: 
```
[2026-03-17T12:04:21Z] runtime: panic: unexpected fault address
[2026-03-17T12:04:21Z] signal SIGSEGV (fault address 0x7f8a2b3c)
[2026-03-17T12:04:21Z] runtime stack:
...
[2026-03-17T12:04:35Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4321 (model-runner) score 987 or sacrifice child
```

jin: that looks like a memory blowup then segfault. which model was hot? model id in headers?

maya (oncall): checking request traces, heavy traffic to model: redwood/llm-13b-v2 (quantized-16). top seq lens ~2048, KV cache growth steady.

eng-runtime: two quick mitigations — 1) route traffic to smaller/quantized-8bit variant (llm-13b-v2-8q) as fallback, 2) enable gateway circuit-breaker to shed new requests to affected pool. can we do 80/20 split and restart pods?

maya (oncall): initiating traffic split and rolling restart of model-runner pool.
```bash
# route 80% to primary, 20% to fallback
redwoodctl route set --service model-serving-runtime --split "primary=80,fallback=20" --fallback-model redwood/llm-13b-v2-8q
# rollout restart (graceful)
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/model-runner --field-selector metadata.name=model-runner
```

carlos: FYI toggled gateway cb for model-serving-runtime -> rejecting new long seq requests (>1024) to preserve mem.

lisa-cs: customer impact: support queue shows ~12 tickets (errors + timeouts) in last 30m, two enterprise customers reported failed requests in US-WEST1. I patched status page with "degraded" and DM'd affected CSMs.

support-ops: putting high-touch customers on a monitored retry policy — will coordinate with eng to verify fallback quality.

sre-ops: keep an eye on evictions. if pods keep getting OOM-killed, we need to scale down concurrency or enable pod memory limits to avoid node-level thrash.

eng-runtime: quick config change to reduce per-process cache: set KV_CACHE_MAX=4GB for model-runner in prod for the affected pool. applying now as canary to two replicas.

maya (oncall): applied KV cache limit to canary pods. restarting them.

Incident timeline update (maya):
- 12:02 UTC: incident-bot alert, 5xx spike
- 12:05 UTC: observed SIGSEGV + OOM in model-runner logs
- 12:08 UTC: enabled 80/20 fallback to llm-13b-v2-8q and gateway CB for long-seq
- 12:12 UTC: applied KV_CACHE_MAX=4GB to canary pods
- 12:20 UTC: rolling restart of remainder of pool started

jin: can we get core dump upload + trace ID list for affected requests? I want to correlate seq length and user payloads.

maya (oncall): uploading core dumps to blob (link: https://s3.redwood/prod/cores/8098765432) and extracted trace_ids: [tr_1182, tr_1183, tr_1190] — uploaded.

eng-runtime: initial telemetry: after split + restarts error rate dropped from 6.4% -> 1.3% over 5m. KV limit seems to prevent immediate evictions. continuing ramp.

lisa-cs: support queue alert now at 4 tickets new in last 10m. informing customers the mitigation is in place and we're monitoring quality.

sre-ops: nodes show one eviction event earlier; no node OOMs currently. good. keeping autoscaler disabled for this pool during mitigation.

maya (oncall): continuing to monitor. can we keep 20% traffic to fallback for 30 minutes then evaluate rollback?

eng-runtime: agreed. also will add a temporary safety net: queue-length limiter + fast-fail on requests >2500 tokens to avoid repeat. pushing change now.

maya (oncall): change applied.

incident-bot: UPDATE: 5xx rate for model-serving-runtime in us-west1 decreased to 1.1% (3m). No new pagers.

maya (oncall): moving to mitigation -> recovery. eng-runtime + sre-ops to follow up for root cause and postmortem. owners: eng-runtime, sre-ops.

eng-runtime: immediate next steps: analyze core dumps for memory corruption, reproduce locally with seq=~2000 and quantized-16 kernels. create regression test.

sre-ops: infra action items: add alert for KV cache growth per-pod, tighten OOM eviction thresholds, add a circuit-breaker rule for long seq by default.

lisa-cs: will do customer roundup + set expectation window.

maya (oncall): thanks all. logging incident in retro tracker and will open follow-ups:
- INCIDENT-8098765432: postmortem (eng-runtime)
- FOLLOWUP-8098765432-1: add KV cache growth alert (sre-ops)
- FOLLOWUP-8098765432-2: fallback rollout test coverage (eng-runtime)

eng-runtime: ack, will draft RCA and mitigation PRs.

maya (oncall): closing pager for now. if rates re-spike re-open. :thumbsup:
